ch1.q: Why did Ranger 7 keep taking pictures while crashing?
options: Each picture was closer and showed more detail
ch1.why: Ranger had no way to land. The closer it got, the sharper its pictures of the surface became.

ch1.q: What did Surveyor 3's scoop help prove?
options: The ground could hold up a landing craft
ch1.why: Testing the soil showed that the surface was firm enough for Apollo.

ch2.q: Why does the Apollo 11 laser reflector still work today?
options: It needs no power at all
ch2.why: It just reflects light straight back, so there is nothing to run out.

ch2.q: Which way is the Moon slowly moving?
ch2.why: Laser timing shows that the Moon drifts about 3.8 centimeters farther away each year.

ch3.q: What does a gravity assist do?
options: Uses a planet's motion to change a spacecraft's speed
Slows a planet down so it can be studied
ch3.why: A spacecraft can borrow a tiny amount of a planet's orbital motion and leave with more speed.

ch3.q: Which planets has only Voyager 2 ever visited?
ch3.why: No other spacecraft has flown past Uranus or Neptune.

ch4.q: What did Viking 1 need to land on Mars?
ch4.why: The thin air slows you down, but not enough. Rockets did the rest.

ch4.q: What did Viking's biology tests conclude?
options: Strange chemistry, but no clear evidence of life
ch4.why: The soil reacted in surprising ways, but no clear sign of living things was found.

ch5.q: How long was Opportunity's mission planned to last?
ch5.why: It was planned for about 90 sols and worked for more than 14 years.

options: A planet-wide dust storm blocked the sun
ch5.why: Solar panels need sunlight. The 2018 storm blocked it.

ch6.q: How many flights was Ingenuity planned to make?
ch6.why: Up to five was the plan. It flew 72 times.

ch6.q: What record did Perseverance set in October 2026?
options: Longest distance driven on another world
ch6.why: It passed Opportunity's record on 11 October 2026.

options: It is the fastest ever rover
It is the farthest human-made object
ch7.why: Nothing we have built has ever gone farther.

ch7.q: Why was the Golden Record made?
options: To tell anyone who finds it about life on Earth
ch7.why: It's a message from Earth, with sounds, music, greetings, and pictures.

m2.q: What did the lunar rover let the astronauts do?
m2.why: The rover carried astronauts, tools, and samples across several kilometres in a single drive.
The real rover was not autonomous. Astronauts sat in it and drove it.

m3.q: Why are craters useful to scientists?
options: They are holes full of water
They show what hit the Moon and roughly when
m3.why: A crater is evidence of an impact. Older surfaces carry more craters and softer edges.

m3.q: Why do scientists compare many Moon rocks?
m3.why: Different rocks formed in different ways, so comparing them reveals how the Moon changed.

m5.q: What did the Apollo 11 seismometer listen for?
m5.why: It measured ground motion from meteoroid impacts and movements inside the Moon.

m5.q: The seismometer stopped sending in 1969. Why does its data still matter?
options: Scientists still study the record it made
m5.why: The instrument is silent, but the record it made is still used to understand the Moon.

a2.q: Astronauts need to carry tools and rocks far from the lander. What should they take?
a2.why: The rover was built to carry two astronauts, their tools, and their samples.

a3.q: You find a rock made of broken pieces pressed together. Which type is it?
a3.why: Breccia forms when fragments are welded together by heat and pressure from impacts.

a4.q: A machine stops working. Which part can still help science?
a4.why: The measurements can outlive the machine that made them.

a5.q: Which sentence best explains why a stopped instrument still matters?
options: It will turn itself back on
It is only useful as a sculpture
Its data is still studied and can teach us new things
a5.why: The value lives in the record and what people learn from it, not in continued operation.

moon.q: Before we start: why might scientists want a rock from the Moon?
moon.why: Moon rocks carry a record of how the Moon formed and changed.

moon.q: Who drove the Apollo lunar rover?
moon.why: The astronauts drove it. This story imagines the rover remembering, but that part is fiction.

moon.q: If a machine stops working, can its data still be useful?
options: Yes, if people keep studying it
moon.why: Data can keep teaching long after the machine goes quiet.
